summary: Implemented src/pcae/core/hpac_verifier.py, the standalone mechanism-neutral HPAC verifier and principal-registry consumption boundary frozen by the .1R.4 planning document. verify_human_authentication() executes HPAC-REQ-054's ten-step fail-closed verification sequence (re-read directly from docs/contracts/HUMAN_PRINCIPAL_AUTHENTICATION_CONTRACT.md section 18) against the existing, independently-verified Layer-1/2 foundation stores (human_principal_registry.py, approval_presentation.py, human_authentication_proof.py, hpac_lifecycle.py). Every authority-bearing input is resolved by the verifier itself through its owning canonical store; only bare identifiers (proof_id, approval_id) are accepted from a caller. AuthenticatedHumanPrincipal is trusted-construction-only (no public constructor) and non-serializable (__reduce__ raises), closing the anti-forgery/anti-transfer threat model by construction; assurance classification is copied from resolved records, never caller-declared, so the deterministic NON-REAL path always remains NON-REAL even with UP/UV both true. One deliberate, documented scope decision: the verifier does not resolve RuntimeInvocationApproval via RuntimeInvocationApprovalStore (no adapter between that record and the HPAC-side CanonicalRuntimeApprovalSubject exists yet, and .1R.4 section 36's own restated no-go-bounded scope does not require it); approval_id is consumed only as an opaque binding key. 27 focused/adversarial tests added (tests/test_hpac_verifier.py), all passing. Full HPAC foundation regression family re-run with zero attributable regressions (fixed-SHA A/B against baseline 817b788a). No runtime_authority.py, runtime_dispatch_permission.py, runtime_invocation_approval_store.py, or Permission Broker file was modified; B1/B7/N1/N2 remain contract closed / implementation open; no real FIDO2; no real protected UI; runtime remains Observed/observe/unavailable; POL-005 unchanged.
derived_correctness: The verifier's ten-step sequence was implemented from a direct re-read of docs/contracts/HUMAN_PRINCIPAL_AUTHENTICATION_CONTRACT.md sections 4-21 (HPAC-REQ-001 through HPAC-REQ-062 region), not solely from .1R.4's own eight-step paraphrase, per the governing prompt's instruction not to rely on the prompt over primary contract text. All eight foundation source modules (hpac_foundation.py, human_principal_registry.py, approval_presentation.py, approval_presentation_deterministic.py, human_authentication_proof.py, human_authenticator.py, human_authenticator_deterministic.py, hpac_lifecycle.py) were read in full before implementation, along with runtime_invocation_approval_store.py and runtime_authority.py's relevant dataclasses, to ground the RuntimeInvocationApprovalStore scope decision in the actual current source shape rather than assumption. The end-to-end test fixture (_Rig in tests/test_hpac_verifier.py) exercises the real fixture-authority stores (registry enrollment, presentation install/present, deterministic challenge/response, canonical proof creation, lifecycle genesis-through-PROOF_VERIFIED) rather than mocking any foundation layer, so a verifier defect could not hide behind a stubbed dependency.
